claim_to_avoid: A fundraising platform bankruptcy proves DAF technology sponsors generally commingle donated funds
directly_supported_observation: Regulatory records document delayed nonprofit remittances and later liquidation
strongest_alternative: Other DAF structures legally place funds with independent sponsor or bank; Flipcause was a fundraiser not a DAF sponsor
currently_justified_conclusion: Do not generalize incidence. Require legal funds flow and bankruptcy-isolation test for each provider.
discriminating_evidence: Bank/custody agreement and a signed fund-owner/service-provider map; independent audited reconciliation

claim_to_avoid: Delayed donations and bankruptcy were caused by a particular technical architecture
directly_supported_observation: Regulator cited missed distributions and registration issues and later bankruptcy occurred
strongest_alternative: Business cashflow, governance, payment contracts, fraud or technology weakness could be causal; no independent root-cause source
currently_justified_conclusion: Observed outcome qualifies for bounded EDF inquiry; technical root cause remains unknown.
discriminating_evidence: Court records, verified bank remittance ledgers, technical forensics, interviews and actual sponsor controls

claim_to_avoid: The notice that data will be deleted proves that all clients lost their data
directly_supported_observation: Company published closure, data access contact and planned deletion
strongest_alternative: Some clients may have exported records, had backup integrations, or received archives
currently_justified_conclusion: High-risk portability exposure, actual loss rate unverified.
discriminating_evidence: Migration completion audit and independent nonprofit customer export verification

claim_to_avoid: The platform failed because its code was poor
directly_supported_observation: Company attributed shutdown to insufficient business growth
strongest_alternative: Sales, market fit, costs, channel dependence, product, engineering or capital may interact; no technical postmortem
currently_justified_conclusion: Business failure observed; engineering cause unproven.
discriminating_evidence: Investor financials product/customer usage and technical failure timelines

claim_to_avoid: Vennfi went out of business and Charityvest DAF assets were sold to Foundation Source
directly_supported_observation: Foundation Source acquired for-profit technology Vennfi, Charityvest remained independent sponsor
strongest_alternative: Product teams changed ownership but charity DAF funds legally stayed with charity
currently_justified_conclusion: Vendor acquisition with charitable sponsorship continuity; no failure inference.
discriminating_evidence: Legal sponsor filings, postdeal continuity and customer consent audit

claim_to_avoid: TIFIN Give ceased to operate after Giving Place sale
directly_supported_observation: April 2025 transaction moved separate Giving Place product to FS; TIFIN maintained its DAF platform
strongest_alternative: Business strategy narrowed vs complete DAF closure
currently_justified_conclusion: Product ownership transfer, not TIFIN closure.
discriminating_evidence: Live TIFIN current offering plus acquisition assignment conditions

claim_to_avoid: The Alaya product already closed on Nov 11, 2026
directly_supported_observation: Parent website schedules retirement for Dec 15, 2026
strongest_alternative: Future plans can change and existing migrations may be in progress
currently_justified_conclusion: As of date a pending sunset, not completed closure.
discriminating_evidence: Review time-stamped vendor update after deadline and migrated product verification

claim_to_avoid: A cybersecurity-related outage proves donor records were breached or permanently lost
directly_supported_observation: Official status disclosed investigation, outage and differing operating vs failed services
strongest_alternative: Precautionary shutdown, incomplete inquiry, no confirmed final impact
currently_justified_conclusion: Only outage and investigation established, root cause and data impact unknown.
discriminating_evidence: Official final incident report, external forensic summary, reconciled donor records after return

claim_to_avoid: SEC and FTC enforcement mean all Blackbaud products today are insecure
directly_supported_observation: US regulators documented historic ransomware disclosures/data safeguards deficiencies
strongest_alternative: Product versions, remediation and audit status may change
currently_justified_conclusion: Historic controls and disclosures failed per regulators; current specific scope needs fresh testing.
discriminating_evidence: Current scoped SOC/penetration reports and verified fixes, not just assurances

claim_to_avoid: Public detailed API docs and SOC2 Type II statement prove best-in-class security
directly_supported_observation: Chariot publicly documents webhook 10 retries and claims Type II
strongest_alternative: Unseen audit scope, real bug rate, security exceptions, subservice and technical debt
currently_justified_conclusion: Greater public API specificity, actual security/control quality not independently validated.
discriminating_evidence: Live sandbox heldout tests and reviewed audit period/exceptions

claim_to_avoid: Open API documentation means sponsor can fully export accounting books with legal receipt provenance
directly_supported_observation: Public contribution/donation endpoints and timestamps visible
strongest_alternative: Other internal restricted records, legal ownership/approval and fund ledger may not be exposed via API
currently_justified_conclusion: Public API capability narrow; complete accounting export untested.
discriminating_evidence: Independent sponsor/bank funded test, complete account data with legal permissions

claim_to_avoid: BridgeFT partnership proves live real-time tax lot correctness for every custodian
directly_supported_observation: Official announcement says multi-custody integrated using BridgeFT API
strongest_alternative: Custody source data cadence, reconciliations, code paths, onboarding, corporate actions remain unknown
currently_justified_conclusion: Public multi-custody claim not proof of real-time or fully correct lot calculations.
discriminating_evidence: Controlled custody feeds and independent tax lot reconciliations across 3 custodians

claim_to_avoid: Product page declaring DAFtech legal sponsor proves US charity EIN and grant legal authority
directly_supported_observation: Product markets sponsor option with brand language
strongest_alternative: Brand name may refer to a service; US legal 501c3 identity and governance unverified
currently_justified_conclusion: Must verify legal sponsor before classifying charitable funds and tax compliance.
discriminating_evidence: Actual sponsor exemption, EIN, legal contract, funding/approval rights

claim_to_avoid: A large transaction volume proves vendor can survive and cannot lose assets
directly_supported_observation: Industry includes high-volume funded systems and failed fundraising platforms
strongest_alternative: Payment throughput is not gross margin, liquidity, donor fund safeguarding or diversified recurring revenue
currently_justified_conclusion: Require audited cashflow, protected charitable assets, provider replaceability and true contract retention.
discriminating_evidence: Company-level financial ratios, safeguarded balances, vendor exit plan

claim_to_avoid: Donations continued during DonorPerfect outage means all downstream records were unaffected
directly_supported_observation: Status shows some donation intake available while CRM/API synchronization stopped
strongest_alternative: Delayed imports, dedupe, consent, reconciliation and acknowledgments still unresolved
currently_justified_conclusion: Payment receipt and CRMs have distinct event boundaries; successful donation is not completed bookkeeping.
discriminating_evidence: Replay queue and compare transaction totals and donor records after verified API recovery

claim_to_avoid: A brand rebrand or legacy product sunset necessarily destroys historical data
directly_supported_observation: Classy became GoFundMe Pro, Bonterra retained CyberGrants, Benevity planned Alaya migration
strongest_alternative: Different companies can preserve data without loss, though migration can also fail
currently_justified_conclusion: Classify event type and test actual record continuity rather than infer outcome from name.
discriminating_evidence: Sample pre/post account export, mapping and signed migration acceptance
